item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is the exact title required by the request and functions as the post’s governing metaphorical thesis.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes unsupported claims about readers’ purchases and how connected-device packaging represents remote servers.","claims":[{"claim":"Owners of connected locks, thermostats, cameras, lights, speakers, or ovens bought those devices without the supporting server being presented on the box as a separate appliance.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do connected-device packages generally omit presenting the supporting server as a separate appliance?"}]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"keep","reason":"This restates the required title’s metaphorical conception of the server as part of the appliance.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence describes a general connected-device architecture not established by the request.","claims":[{"claim":"Connected home products generally consist of both a physical object in the home and a vendor-operated cloud service.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which connected home products depend on a vendor-operated cloud service as a functional component?"}]},{"id":"p2s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The first clause expressly defines the author’s use of “appliance,” but the explanation asserts that devices, apps, accounts, and remote computers collectively performed advertised functions.","claims":[{"claim":"Connected home products are sold as systems comprising a device, app, account, and remote computers that collectively perform the advertised job.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"For which connected home products do the device, app, account, and remote computers collectively perform the advertised function?"}]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"keep","reason":"This introduces the vendor cloud-service closure expressly supplied as the scenario the request requires the post to cover.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"keep","reason":"“Perhaps” clearly signals an imagined possibility in the supplied shutdown scenario.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"keep","reason":"“Perhaps” clearly signals an imagined possibility rather than reporting an actual device outcome.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence asserts that a cloud shutdown causes a specified range of feature losses, none of which the request identifies.","claims":[{"claim":"Closing a connected-device cloud service can eliminate remote access, schedules, notifications, voice control, shared accounts, automation, history, security updates, or the ability to complete setup.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which listed connected-device features have been shown to stop working when vendor cloud services close, and for which designs?"}]},{"id":"p3s5","status":"keep","reason":"The variation by design is inherent in asking which features stop, and the conditional conclusion follows without an external premise: a function that must obtain remote permission or instructions cannot continue completely from the retained physical box alone.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s6","status":"keep","reason":"This is a qualified evaluative characterization of the shutdown’s effect on the buyer’s understood bargain.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The question presupposes a prediction about how vendors are likely to respond.","claims":[{"claim":"A vendor that closes a connected-device service is likely to defend the shutdown by distinguishing ownership of the device from continuation of the online service.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do vendors commonly make this device-versus-service distinction when closing connected-device cloud services?"}]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"reject","reason":"This presents attributed vendor wording or a vendor position that is absent from the request and is not explicitly framed as invented dialogue.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is an evaluative rejection of the preceding distinction and adds no independently checkable premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a conditional definitional inference: if the promised function required the server at sale, the server contributed to that function.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s5","status":"keep","reason":"The author coins a rhetorical label and uses a coherent machine-and-gear analogy to restate the supplied scenario of vendor-retained control over functionality after sale.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes an unsupported universal claim about companies’ ability to promise indefinite operation.","claims":[{"claim":"No company can promise to operate a service forever.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Is it accurate, and in what contractual or practical sense, that no company can promise indefinite service operation?"}]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence states four external propositions about operating costs, business survival, changing standards, and the safety of aging systems.","claims":[{"claim":"Operating servers costs money.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What ongoing costs are ordinarily incurred in operating servers for connected-device services?"},{"claim":"Businesses sometimes fail.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes business failure as a relevant cause of connected-device service shutdowns?"},{"claim":"Security standards change over time.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which security standards relevant to connected devices have changed over time?"},{"claim":"Aging computer systems can become dangerous.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Under what conditions do aging connected-device systems create security or safety dangers?"}]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative inference: conceding possible reasons for shutdown does not logically determine who ought to bear its cost.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s4","status":"keep","reason":"The rhetorical question makes a value argument within the supplied dependency scenario; the vendor’s architectural choice and continued cooperation are conditional restatements of that dependency.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s5","status":"keep","reason":"This states the authorial position that indefinite cloud operation is not being demanded; it is not biographical evidence or an external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s6","status":"keep","reason":"This states a normative expectation for an exit that respects the original bargain, with an evaluative contrast to vendor cost minimization.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s1","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence makes universal claims about household durable-goods purchasing and buyers’ market expectations.","claims":[{"claim":"All buyers of household durable goods expect ownership to outlast the seller’s willingness to support the product.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Is this expectation broadly shared by buyers of household durable goods, and how has it been measured or documented?"}]},{"id":"p6s2","status":"keep","reason":"The first clause is a recommendation, and “tenancy” is an evaluative analogy for ownership subject to continuing vendor control.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s3","status":"disclose","reason":"The remote fuse box is a permissible metaphor for vendor control, but the sentence also generalizes about the costs and risks borne by connected-device buyers.","claims":[{"claim":"Connected-device buyers generally pay the purchase price and electricity costs, maintain the required network, and bear the physical risks of the device.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which purchase, operating, maintenance, and physical risks are generally borne by owners of connected home devices?"},{"claim":"Vendors of cloud-dependent connected devices retain remote power to disable important product functions.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"For which connected-device architectures can the vendor remotely disable important functions by withdrawing service?"}]},{"id":"p6s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is figurative language mapping the vendor’s departure and service shutdown onto pulling the previously introduced remote fuse.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is an evaluative comparison of the supplied shutdown arrangement to a lease with a concealed termination mechanism.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is the conceptual conclusion that local operation reallocates control from the remote vendor to the owner, derived from the meaning of local operation.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s2","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence defines local operability and gives illustrative capabilities that follow from each expressly described local design rather than claiming every real device has them.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s3","status":"keep","reason":"The cloud example is framed as a possibility, while the second clause is a normative recommendation that core operation not depend on it.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a conditional inference and analogy: if local core functions survive service closure, the lost cloud function is accessory rather than the entire machine.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a general conceptual consequence of local operation: functions not dependent on vendor service remain under local control before a shutdown as well.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s2","status":"keep","reason":"The listed vendor actions form imagined contingencies, and continued use follows conditionally for a device whose relevant operation is genuinely local.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s3","status":"keep","reason":"This states the author’s evaluative acceptance of optional services and adds no external descriptive premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s4","status":"keep","reason":"This identifies, as a value judgment, where the author believes the problem begins.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical classification derived from whether a dependency is optional and who controls the unavoidable dependency.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s1","status":"keep","reason":"This introduces the author’s proposed policy demands and makes no external descriptive assertion.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s2","status":"keep","reason":"All three clauses are recommendations for product operation, setup, and documentation.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative demand for shutdown planning, followed by proposed ways vendors could satisfy it.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s4","status":"keep","reason":"This clarifies the scope of the author’s argument and makes no external factual claim.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative design principle against coupling a buyer’s property failure to seller failure.","claims":[]},{"id":"p10s1","status":"disclose","reason":"Although phrased metaphorically, the sentence generalizes that a connected appliance includes both a physical object and a remote service.","claims":[{"claim":"Connected appliances generally depend on both a physical object and a remotely operated service.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Which categories of connected appliances depend on a remotely operated service in addition to the physical object?"}]},{"id":"p10s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The conclusion about accounting for both components is normative, but it rests on an unsupported claim about what connected-appliance sales pitches include.","claims":[{"claim":"Sales pitches for connected appliances include both the physical device and the remote service as parts of the offered product.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"Do connected-appliance marketing and sales materials generally present both device and remote-service capabilities as part of the product offer?"}]},{"id":"p10s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a proposed rule permitting necessary server closure while demanding preservation of appliance functionality.","claims":[]},{"id":"p10s4","status":"keep","reason":"The first clause repeats the required metaphorical thesis, and the second is a definitional inference that local operation preserves appliance functions when the server is unavailable.","claims":[]}]}
